description: TESPy (Thermal Engineering Systems in Python) is an open-source toolkit for simulating thermal engineering plants such as power plants including organic Rankine cycles, heat pumps, refrigeration machines, district heating and HVAC systems, and energy balances of industrial processes. It was started by Francesco Witte and is part of the Open Energy Modelling Framework (oemof) community, while also usable standalone. It computes stationary operation to design a plant and then simulates off-design behaviour from component characteristics, with basic components such as turbines, pumps, compressors, heat exchangers, pipes, mixers and splitters and advanced heat exchanger and drum components. The method is location-independent. It is a Python package for Python 3.11 or later, installable from PyPI, documented on Read the Docs, with about 100 tagged releases (latest v0.11.2) and versions archived on Zenodo, under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: it models steady states, not dynamics, and results depend on component characteristics supplied by the user. Simulation uses are design and off-design analysis of heat pumps, power plants and district heating plants. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
